As the Internet was yet to be widely used, rumor was a dominant channel for the rapid spread of information, and every day brought word of new breakthroughs. paragraphs.source_en: We were particularly fortunate at Oxford: Michael Green had recently visited to lecture on string theory, so many of us became familiar with the theory's basic ideas and essential claims. And impressive claims they were. In a nutshell, here is what the theory said: Take any piece of matter-a block of ice, a chunk of rock, a slab of iron -and imagine cutting it in half, then cutting one of the pieces in half again, and on and on; imagine continually cutting the material into ever smaller pieces. Some 2,500 years ago, the ancient Greeks had posed the problem of determining the finest, uncuttable, indivisible ingredient that would be the end product of such a procedure. In our age we have learned that sooner or later you come to atoms, but atoms are not the answer to the Greeks' question, because they can be cut into finer con stituents. Atoms can be split.
